title: The free 'weigh what this grief asks' preview at the Kings' Rest hearth-stone named only the Keeper's Key ('the Keeper's Key is yours -- lay it on the hearth-stone') as the way to rest the old court outright, but omitted the equally valid 'speak the three verses over the court' option that was on the very same action menu -- a player trusting the weigh preview alone would not know verses could rest it without spending the Key (which the item's own flavor text says is also needed later at Coldpass).
where: The Kings' Rest — the Old Court (Hollowbrook) — second 'weigh' after gathering both key and verses

evidence.quote: The second 'weigh what this grief asks' at the Old Court, taken after already holding the Keeper's Key and all three downs verses, described only the Key path as ready ('the Keeper's Key is yours — lay it on the hearth-stone') and never mentioned that the three-verses option (also fully unlocked in the very same action menu, no missing-item caveat) was equally ready.

The free 'weigh what this grief asks' preview at the Kings' Rest hearth-stone named only the Keeper's Key ('the Keeper's Key is yours -- lay it on the hearth-stone') as the way to rest the old court outright, but omitted the equally valid 'speak the three verses over the court' option that was on the very same action menu -- a player trusting the weigh preview alone would not know verses could rest it without spending the Key (which the item's own flavor text says is also needed later at Coldpass).
